candidates.where: t1 — 'Marcia et Marcus in Roma habitant ... Filius eorum Quintus in ludo discit. Filia eorum Claudia domi manet. Servus aquam portat.' / t3 — 'Was ist ein Atrium in einem römischen Haus? ... Das Atrium war der zentrale offene Innenhof des römischen Hauses, oft mit einem Wasserbecken — dem impluvium.'
candidates.figure: Cutaway or simplified isometric view of a Roman domus showing: entrance corridor (fauces), atrium with impluvium (small pool), tablinum (master's room opening off atrium), and garden (hortus) at the rear. Figures at scale for proportion but not labelled in the image itself.
candidates.why: The worksheet asks pupils to translate a text about a Roman family AND answer about the atrium. An architectural cross-section/cutaway makes the spatial vocabulary (atrium, impluvium, domus) immediately intuitive and grounds the translation task in a visible world. It also feeds t5's compare-and-contrast task (Roman house vs. today).
candidates.recipe_or_reason: Roman domus isometric cutaway. No embedded Latin or German labels in the image (all labels in worksheet text below the figure). Architecturally plausible but stylised; no photo. Anachronism risk: moderate — instruct no modern elements (no glass windows, no chimneys). Vetter checks: correct impluvium position, compluvium opening above, tablinum open to atrium.
candidates.content_risk: medium — architectural illustration has factual content; vetter must check impluvium placement is correct and no anachronistic details (electricity, modern furniture) slip in
candidates.caption: Eine römische Domus: Das Atrium mit Impluvium im Zentrum des Hauses.

candidates.subject: Latein
candidates.worksheet: c0060 — Nomen und Kasus: Nominativ und Akkusativ
candidates.where: t3 — 'Übersetze die folgenden lateinischen Sätze ins Deutsche. Unterstreiche dabei das Subjekt (Nominativ) und kreise das Objekt (Akkusativ) ein. 1. Puella servum videt. 2. Servus viam longam intrat. 3. Dominus puellam laudat.'
candidates.figure: Three simple comic-strip panels illustrating the three sentences: (1) a girl looking at a slave figure; (2) a man walking onto/entering a wide road; (3) a man gesturing approvingly toward a girl. Stick-figure or line-art style — no text inside the panels.
candidates.why: The core difficulty of this kasus worksheet is understanding who acts (Nominativ subject) on whom (Akkusativ object) — a purely grammatical abstraction. Small action scenes make the semantic roles concrete before the grammatical terms are applied, supporting the understand→apply progression from t3 onward.
candidates.recipe_or_reason: Three minimal comic panels, line-art. Roman-ish dress (simple tunics) but non-specific era markers. Directional arrows of gaze/action implicit in the scene composition. No text bubbles, no labels in image. Simple enough that diffusion is unlikely to introduce garbled text.
candidates.content_risk: low — line-art action panels; no factual claims; vetter checks: consistent simple Roman tunic style, no anachronisms, actions clearly directional
candidates.caption: Wer handelt? Wer wird betroffen? Erkenne Nominativ und Akkusativ in den Bildern.
